paragraphs.text: Red foxes have lived in British cities since at least the 1930s, when new suburbs with large gardens offered food and shelter. A study in Bristol, which tracked foxes with small radio collars, found that most urban foxes do not travel far: a typical adult spent its entire life within an area of about one square kilometre. The researchers were surprised, however, to find that young males often left home in their first winter and could move more than ten kilometres, sometimes crossing busy roads and railway lines to reach new territory.
